q1: SELECT b1.name AS bar1, b2.name AS bar2 FROM bar AS b1, bar AS b2 WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT s1.beer FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND s2.beer = s1.beer)) AND EXISTS(SELECT s2.beer FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND s1.beer = s2.beer))
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT b1.name AS bar1, b2.name AS bar2 FROM bar AS b1, bar AS b2 WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT s1.beer FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND s2.beer = s1.beer)) AND EXISTS(SELECT s2.beer FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND s1.beer = s2.beer))
counterexample: INSERT INTO Bar (name, address) VALUES ('BarA', 'AddressA'), ('BarB', 'AddressB'); INSERT INTO Beer (name, brewer) VALUES ('X', 'BrewerX'), ('Y', 'BrewerY'), ('Z', 'BrewerZ'); INSERT INTO Serves (bar, beer, price) VALUES ('BarA', 'X', 5.00), ('BarA', 'Y', 4.00), ('BarB', 'Y', 4.50), ('BarB', 'Z', 6.00);
explanation: Q1 is intended to find bars that serve a unique set of beers (no other bar serves the same beer) and another bar that serves a unique set of beers (no other bar serves the same beer) but with at least one beer that the first bar does not serve. Q2, however, simply selects all bars from the Bar table. The two queries are not semantically equivalent because Q1 has a complex condition that filters bars based on the uniqueness of the beers they serve, while Q2 does not have any conditions and simply returns all bars.
counterexample_dsp: Create two bars, BarA and BarB, where BarA serves beer X and beer Y, and BarB serves beer Y and beer Z. BarA should be in the result of Q1 because it serves a unique set of beers (X and Y) that no other bar serves. BarB should not be in the result of Q1 because it does not serve a unique set of beers (Y is served by BarA). Q2, on the other hand, will return both BarA and BarB.
